WITH pair_avg AS (
  SELECT f.orderslink, u.acctscope, AVG(f.feerate) AS avg_feerate
  FROM fees f
  JOIN orders o ON f.orderslink = o.recordvault
  JOIN users u ON o.userlink = u.userstamp
  GROUP BY f.orderslink, u.acctscope
),
overall AS (
  SELECT AVG(avg_feerate) AS mean_avg FROM pair_avg
),
excess AS (
  SELECT p.orderslink, p.acctscope, p.avg_feerate, p.avg_feerate - o.mean_avg AS excess
  FROM pair_avg p CROSS JOIN overall o
  WHERE p.avg_feerate > o.mean_avg
),
ranked AS (
  SELECT orderslink, acctscope, avg_feerate, excess,
         RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY acctscope ORDER BY excess DESC) AS scope_rank
  FROM excess
)
SELECT orderslink, acctscope, avg_feerate, excess, scope_rank
FROM ranked
WHERE scope_rank <= 3
ORDER BY acctscope, scope_rank, orderslink;

assumptions.assumption: The mean of all pair averages is computed over every pair after the inner joins, including pairs whose average is NULL being excluded by AVG (pairs with only NULL feerates yield NULL averages and are ignored).
Ties in excess within a scope share a rank (RANK), so more than 3 rows can appear if ties occur at the boundary.

alternatives.interpretation: Ties broken arbitrarily so exactly 3 pairs per scope are returned (ROW_NUMBER instead of RANK).

assumptions.assumption: The mean of all pair averages is the unweighted mean of the per-pair averages, computed over all pairs from the inner joins (pairs whose feerate is all NULL are ignored), not over the whole scope or over individual fee rows.
Ties in excess within a scope are broken by orderslink, using ROW_NUMBER, so each scope returns at most 3 rows.
orders.recordvault and users.userstamp are unique, so the joins do not duplicate fee rows.
